kept.title: Incorrect handling of objects with $class but null $ in writeObject
kept.explanation: The condition in proto.writeObject's initial if statement was changed from checking if the object is null or undefined, or if it has a $class string and a null/undefined $ property, to only checking if the object is null or undefined. This removes the special handling case where an object with a $class and null $ value is encoded as null. Without this, such objects will not encode as null but will attempt serialization as objects, leading to errors or incorrect encoding.
kept.suggestion: Restore original check for (is.nullOrUndefined(obj) || (is.string(obj.$class) && is.nullOrUndefined(obj.$))) in proto.writeObject to correctly encode objects that have a $class and null $ as null.
kept.failureAfterChange: Encoding an object like { $class: 'xxx', $: null } no longer results in the encoded null ('N') indicator. Instead, the encoder attempts to serialize it as an object, causing errors or corrupted output.

verdicts.reason: The change removed handling for objects with a $class property but null $ property in proto.writeObject. Previously, such objects were encoded as null, but now they are not. This introduces a real defect: these objects no longer encode correctly and may cause errors or corrupted output. Hence, the finding correctly identifies a defect introduced by the change.
